clue.text: Gossip with Russell, kind of loathsome chap

parts.note: to gossip is to chatter idly, to natter
a Jack Russell is a kind of terrier, so the kind of Russell is a Jack

explanation.surface: A gossiping terrier owner is dismissed as a nasty piece of work.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is a European toad, and calling someone a toad means they are loathsome, hence the cryptic definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a species of toad, and a toad is slang for a repellent person.

clue.text: Where in Umbria a southern river rises

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the word for the river is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: the Isis is the name of the Thames at Oxford

explanation.surface: Someone asks where in Umbria a river from the south has its source.
explanation.definitionFit: The hill town of St Francis lies in the Italian region of Umbria.

clue.text: The Opposition leader has two notes for him

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its opening letter, here of Opposition

parts.note: do and re are the first two notes of the sol-fa scale
do and re are the first two notes of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The head of the Opposition boasts a couple of musical notes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Opposition leader' reads as a political figure, but it gives THE plus the first letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: A man's first name, so the answer can stand for a male person, him.

clue.text: Crazy artist built shed in rotten elm

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist

indicators.note: in signals the shed goes inside the jumbled elm letters
rotten signals that the letters of elm are spoiled and rearranged

parts.note: a shack is a rough shed

explanation.surface: A mad painter has put up a hut inside a decaying elm tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rotten' turns ELM into MLE, and 'in' puts SHACK inside it: M-SHACK-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tumbledown and rickety is crazy in the sense of lopsided and unsound.

clue.text: Did Lang break down, with confusing outcome?

indicators.note: breaking the words down signals their letters are taken apart and reassembled

explanation.surface: A man called Lang collapses, and the result is muddled.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle someone's head is to confuse them, so muddling and confusing are synonyms.

clue.text: She named the insect, she did

definitions.text: She named the insect, she did

parts.words: She named the insect, she did
parts.note: the green bush-cricket's name is said to imitate its call, a girl's name followed by 'did', so the girl gave the insect half its name

explanation.surface: A woman gave an insect her name, and did so.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's name forming the first part of the North American bush-cricket's name, completed by 'did'.

clue.text: Get ailment or perhaps die from something in the water

parts.note: flu is a common ailment

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of die are offered in another arrangement

explanation.surface: You may fall ill or even die from something in your drinking water.
explanation.definitionFit: This compound is added to tap water to protect teeth, so it is a substance in the water.

clue.text: Broadcast order to the plant

parts.note: broadcast is scattering seed, so an order to scatter seed of this weed, addressed to the plant itself, gives its name

explanation.surface: A radio announcement is made to a factory.
explanation.definitionFit: A common weed with milky sap and thistle-like leaves, whose name splits as a command to scatter seed of it.

clue.text: Bright youth the Americans moon around with!

definitions.meaning: the Greek sun god, the type of radiant young male beauty
the NASA programme whose craft took Americans round and onto the moon

explanation.surface: A clever young man and the Americans mope about together.
explanation.definitionFit: The god of light, a handsome youth, also named the US space programme that flew crews around the moon.

clue.text: Respected Italian family connected with E Mediterranean

parts.note: the Este were a ruling family of Ferrara
Med is the short name for the Mediterranean

explanation.surface: An Italian dynasty linked to the eastern Mediterranean was held in high regard.
explanation.definitionFit: Held in high regard, admired and looked up to.

clue.text: Knock Jack down, the loafer

parts.note: to lay is to strike, as in lay into someone
a jack (jack tar) is a sailor, as is AB, able seaman
a boxer knocked down for the count is out

explanation.surface: Floor Jack, the idle good-for-nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knock Jack down' reads as one action, but gives three pieces in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A lazy idler who does no work, a shirker.

clue.text: The old queen was so idle

parts.note: did stands in for a verb, as in 'so she did', so it serves for was
idle means doing nothing, and O is zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A former queen is said to have been lazy.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as 'did nothing', DID plus O (zero), which is to be idle.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary queen of Carthage who loved Aeneas, a monarch of ancient times.

clue.text: Violated dead secret maybe

indicators.note: maybe signals the letters of dead secret are one possible rearrangement

explanation.surface: A secret about the dead has been broken.
explanation.definitionFit: Treating something sacred with violent disrespect is profaning it.

clue.text: Girl gets round to party by car with current date

parts.note: Ann is a girl's name
O is round in shape
a do is a party
the Mini is a small British car

explanation.surface: A young woman drives a car to a party with a lift.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin phrase 'in the year of the Lord', abbreviated AD, is the label of the current era of dates.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin label of the Christian era, used in every present-day year.

clue.text: Hated, perhaps, to look at this type of insect

indicators.note: perhaps signals the letters of Hated are offered in another arrangement

parts.note: to watch is to look at

explanation.surface: An insect so loathed that one shudders to look at it.
explanation.definitionFit: A wood-boring beetle whose ticking was once thought to foretell a death.

clue.text: Darts king stares rudely about him

indicators.note: about signals the rearranged letters go round the king
rudely signals the letters of stares are roughly thrown about

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A darts-playing king is the target of rude stares.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rudely' turns STARES into STREAS, and 'about' puts it round K.
explanation.definitionFit: To dart is to move like a flash, to streak.

clue.text: City on the Danube, forming river bastion

indicators.note: forming signals the letters of bastion are shaped into something new

explanation.surface: A Danube city has a riverside fortification.
explanation.definitionFit: Old name for Regensburg, a Bavarian city on the Danube.

clue.text: Object found in torn clothing

indicators.note: found in signals one piece placed inside another

parts.note: rent means torn, the past of rend
an aim is an object or purpose

explanation.surface: Something discovered among ripped garments.
explanation.definitionFit: A literary word for garments, attire.

clue.text: The Boy you'll find in the ranks of death, said Moore

parts.words: The Boy you'll find in the ranks of death, said Moore
parts.note: Thomas Moore's song begins with this young singer going to war, and says 'in the ranks of death you'll find him'

explanation.surface: A poet named Moore wrote of a lad found among the dead.

clue.text: Get timing wrong so almost fail to keep appointment

indicators.note: almost means one letter short at the end of the word

parts.note: to miss an appointment is to fail to keep it
a date is an appointment

explanation.surface: Being late nearly makes you miss a meeting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' takes the last S off MISS.

clue.text: Sepia of Dickensian sea-captain as swimmer/

parts.note: Captain Cuttle is the old seaman in Dickens's Dombey and Son
a fish is a swimmer

explanation.surface: A brown-tinted picture of a Dickens sea-captain swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sepia' looks like a photo's tint, but it is the Latin genus name of the mollusc, which gave the ink its name.

clue.text: Keep this bouquet clean to ' avoid trouble

clue.text: Series bearing on Hertfordshire town

Tring is a market town in Hertfordshire, a county north of London

clue.text: Read news-letters and corresponded

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for registered

indicators.note: at first signals the opening letter of Personal

clue.text: A stimulant for the starlet?

parts.note: a steroid is a drug used to boost performance
